Privacy policy

How we handle account details, community contributions, and information from your browser.

Effective and last updated November 10, 2026

The essentials

  • You can read the trackers and Catch Up without creating an account.
  • Your sign-in email and individual voting identity are not shown on the public board.
  • Approved submissions, vote totals, and deliberately public moderator comments can be read by anyone.
  • Withdrawing a submission hides it from the board. Its saved text and history remain until removed by the operator.

Questions or a privacy request? Email chris@holtsnidertech.com.

1. Who operates this site

Infierno Liberado is operated by Christopher Holtsnider through Holtsnider Tech in the United States. It is an independent community project, not an official Team17 service.

This policy covers Infierno Liberado at hllv-bug-track.onrender.com, including the bug tracker, content tracker, Catch Up, and community account and submission features. Other DailyFlyer themes and linked websites have their own practices.

You can contact the operator at chris@holtsnidertech.com. Please include “Infierno Liberado privacy request” in the subject.

2. Information we handle

Accounts and sign-in

If you register, we use your email address and a site password through Supabase Auth. Supabase stores a salted password hash, along with an account identifier, verification status, and authentication records. Sign-in sessions and security records can include timestamps, IP addresses, browser information, and account or session identifiers.

Verification, sign-in, and password-recovery messages use email delivery services. Private replies from moderators currently do not trigger email notifications.

Community contributions

We store what you submit: the title, type of contribution, description, requested outcome, optional related issue, and replies. We also store account associations, votes, wording versions, publication status, moderation decisions, timestamps, and the policy version acknowledged when submitting. Account-based counters help limit repeated requests and submissions.

Please keep contributions about the game. Do not include passwords, verification codes, private correspondence, or personal details about yourself or someone else.

Public sources and messages to us

The trackers use public announcements and selected public community reports. Records may contain public names or usernames, quotations, source links, and dates. If you contact us by email, we receive the address, message, and any attachments you choose to send.

Website requests

Hosting, authentication, and delivery providers process technical requests to operate and secure the site. These requests can include IP addresses, browser details, requested resources, timestamps, and diagnostic information. The main tracker currently initializes its Supabase connection and loads a library from jsDelivr even when you have not signed in or opened the community section.

3. How we use it

  • Provide sign-in, account verification, recovery, and the features you choose to use.
  • Review contributions, respond privately, publish approved wording, and count support votes.
  • Maintain a record of wording changes and moderation decisions, prevent duplicate actions, and limit abuse.
  • Operate and troubleshoot the site, maintain source-based tracker records, and respond to questions and privacy requests.

We do not sell personal information or use it for targeted advertising. The current application does not run advertising trackers, behavioral analytics, or session replay. Provider security and operational logging is separate from those activities.

4. What is public and private

Public: curated tracker records, approved submission wording and related details, aggregate vote totals, and comments a moderator deliberately posts as public. Published material may be indexed, copied, or shared by others. Text can identify someone even when their account details are omitted.

Restricted: pending submissions and private conversations are available to their author and authorized site moderators through the application. Publishing a submission does not make its private conversation public. The application restricts ordinary members to their own private submissions. Moderator practice records are separate from public contributions.

The public board does not display sign-in email addresses, individual voter identities, or private account identifiers. We still retain the internal connection between an account and its submissions or votes.

Authorized project administrators and service providers may access information as needed for administration, support, and security. We may also disclose information when required by law or necessary to address abuse or protect people and the service. Submissions are not end-to-end encrypted; authorized moderators and database administrators can read them.

5. Providers and storage locations

Render
Serves the public website and published tracker files through a global content delivery network. Render privacy policy ↗
Supabase
Provides account authentication and the PostgreSQL database for community records. The primary project is hosted in AWS Oregon, United States (us-west-2). Authentication email delivery also involves email service providers. Supabase privacy policy ↗
jsDelivr
Delivers the Supabase JavaScript library used by the main tracker. Loading it sends a request to that provider. jsDelivr privacy policy ↗
GitHub
Hosts site code and published tracker material used for deployment. Private account records and community conversations are stored in the database, rather than published as site files. Earlier public tracker versions may remain in repository history. GitHub privacy statement ↗

The Supabase project also supports other Holtsnider Tech applications, currently New Passage and Farwake. Project administration is shared. Farwake uses separate captain-passport credentials rather than the email accounts used here. Sharing the project does not make your private Infierno submissions visible to ordinary users of those applications. A request to remove an email account needs to consider any other services using that same account.

Primary database location does not mean all processing stays in Oregon. Providers may process logs, technical information, email delivery, support requests, or account administration in other countries. Supabase’s current data-residency information ↗ describes these exceptions, including operational logs stored in the EU.

The site uses HTTPS, and Supabase documents encryption in transit and at rest. These measures do not guarantee complete security or prevent authorized administrative access.

6. Browser storage and your choices

  • Appearance: your light or dark preference is saved in this browser.
  • Sign-in: session-only browser storage is the default, with coordination between open tabs for this site. Choosing “Keep me signed in on this device” uses persistent browser storage. Session tokens and account/session details are stored there; the application does not save your password there.
  • Catch Up: selected date, familiarity, role, and topic can appear after the # in a shareable URL. They are not an account record of your actual game activity. Browser history and anyone receiving the link may retain those selections.
  • Drafts and private views: the community interface does not deliberately save submission drafts or private conversations in browser storage. Unsaved form text can be lost when you leave the page.

Use remembered sign-in only on a device you trust, and sign out on shared devices. You can clear site data in your browser to remove local preferences and stored sign-in details. Clearing browser data does not delete your account, submissions, or other server records. Browser restore features and password managers have their own behavior.

These features use browser storage rather than advertising cookies. Infrastructure providers may have their own necessary security mechanisms; this policy does not promise that no cookies or technical identifiers are ever used.

7. Retention and removal

There is currently no automatic expiry or deletion schedule for community records. Account details, submissions, previous wording, private replies, votes, and moderation history can remain in the project until the operator removes them. Revision, withdrawal, and account removal have different effects.

  • Editing a published submission sends the revised wording back for review.
  • Withdrawing a submission removes it from public display and makes its conversation read-only. Saved text, prior versions, and history remain.
  • Removing your support vote removes the current vote. Votes associated with older wording can remain in historical records.
  • Moderator practice has its own deletion control; it does not delete an account or unrelated records.

Public tracker snapshots and repository history can retain earlier published material. Withdrawal or a correction cannot retract search caches, screenshots, or copies made by others.

Messages sent to our contact address are handled through the operator’s email service and may remain in the mailbox until removed. The email provider may retain separate copies or technical records under its own retention practices.

Provider logs and any backups have separate retention and deletion behavior. The site does not promise immediate removal from every historical copy. If you request deletion, we need to consider associated records, shared account use, and any limited information that must be retained for security, legal obligations, or resolving disputes.

8. Privacy requests

Email chris@holtsnidertech.com to ask about your information, request access or a copy, correct information, request deletion, or raise a privacy concern. Include your account email if relevant and a link or description of the affected record.

Requests are handled manually. The site currently has no self-service full account-deletion or complete data-export tool. We may need to verify that you control the account before disclosing or removing private records. Do not send passwords, sign-in links, or verification codes.

Depending on the laws that apply to you, you may have additional rights, including rights to object to or restrict processing and to complain to a privacy regulator. Use the contact above to explain your request. Any applicable legal requirements govern how it is handled.

9. External sites and policy changes

Links to game publishers, community discussions, videos, and other websites take you to services with their own privacy practices. Their content and policies are outside this site’s control.

We will update this page and its date when these practices change. The dated policy is retained in the site’s source history. This notice describes how the service handles information; acknowledging it is separate from choosing to submit wording for public publication.
